title: Acute low back pain
priority: Leading cause of disability under age 45; imaging overuse is a known problem.

layer0.label: Red flags
layer0.detail: New urinary retention or overflow incontinence, loss of anal tone or fecal incontinence, saddle anesthesia, progressive leg weakness; also cancer history, infection, fracture risk.

gate.label: Cauda equina features or severe or progressive deficit
No red flags
gate.detail: No imaging for uncomplicated pain under 6 weeks.

gate_note: Most uncomplicated acute low back pain needs no imaging.

ces.text: Bladder, bowel or saddle symptoms, or progressive weakness.

mech.text: No red flags makes uncomplicated pain likely.

steps.title: No imaging if no red flags
steps.description: All imaging is rated usually not appropriate.

mech.text: Half of patients recover in 2 weeks and 90% by 3 months.

steps.title: MRI
steps.timing: Red flags, or no improvement after 6 weeks
steps.description: Modality of choice for most patients who need imaging.

ces.text: MRI evaluates the cauda equina better than CT.

malig.text: MRI is preferred when malignancy is suspected.

infx.text: MRI is the modality of choice for most patients who need imaging.

do_not_rely.text: Imaging every patient; it does not improve outcomes in uncomplicated pain.

ces.no_rule_note: No red flags means it is not pursued; MRI decides when flags are present.

do_not_rely.text: Malignancy red flags as proven; most lack empirical support.

malig.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

infx.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

fx.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

mech.no_rule_note: What remains when red flags are absent.

gaps.title: Red-flag evidence
gaps.text: Many red flags lack empirical support; validated thresholds are missing.
